title: bot.input
description:
Interrupt signal observed by an active bot.

This is how something that happens to a bot becomes an occasion for it. A device reports
its own state change here; the body grants the turn on device identity alone and cognition
decides what, if anything, the change is worth doing about.

anyOf.description: Stable reference for a device. Only devices may become focused.

target_device.description: Stable reference for the device that produced or owns the input. A device does not know what its bot files it under, so it leaves this unset and the body resolves the device from the envelope source — the nerve the signal arrived on.
target_device.title: Target Device

priority.description: How insistent this signal is, where 0 is the highest priority and 10 is the lowest. Like loudness, this belongs to the signal rather than to whatever produced it; a source that does not distinguish leaves it at the ordinary default.
priority.title: Priority

event.description: Canonical HSM event name that emitted this upstream payload.
event.title: Event

data.description: Complete typed payload emitted by the upstream event.
data.title: Data

id.description: Upstream HSM event correlation id, when the emitter stamped one.
id.title: Id

source.description: Upstream HSM event source identity, when stamped by its producer.
source.title: Source

target.description: Upstream HSM event target identity, when stamped for delivery.
target.title: Target

observation.description: Typed product that caused this input. It preserves the producing event's concrete payload and envelope provenance without reducing the observation to an event-name string and untyped JSON bag.

participants.description: Who took part in the observation, as the device that observed it stamped them; the body hands them to cognition unchanged. Empty when the device knows no one (a ring, a link coming up).

items.description: Someone who took part in a stimulus: an opaque, producer-stable identity reference and the role it played (source: who produced it; target: who it was addressed to).

ref.description: Opaque, producer-stable identity such as a phone number, an app person id, or a chat handle. Never a display name chosen by the bot.
ref.title: Ref

role.description: source: who produced the stimulus (speaker, sender). target: who it was addressed to.
role.title: Role

own.description: True when the producer knows this participant is the bot itself, for example the bot's own voice heard back or the voice it spoke with. Stamped only by that producer; never inferred.
own.title: Own

resembles.description: For an identity its producer made just now (nobody it knew): the known identities it resembles, best first, at most 3. Stamped only by that producer; never a link.

items.description: A known identity this new one resembles: its ref and how similar the two are (-1..1). Perception data only: it links nothing, and it is never a print.

ref.description: The ref of the known identity, as its producer stamps it.
ref.title: Ref

similarity.description: How similar the two are, -1..1; higher is more alike.
similarity.title: Similarity

resembles.title: Resembles

items.title: Participant

participants.title: Participants
